title: Reading Landscape fuller ordinary wording independent semantic check
method: Compared every complete mixed candidate with its exact English source and inspected every localized clause and retained English segment. Checks are semantic and bounded, not fluent-speaker approval.

rows.sourceEnglishExact: Watch your own site before choosing where to place tender crops, trees, or buildings.

currentLearnerExact.text: Sheba sebaka sa hao pele u khetha where to place tender crops, trees, or buildings.

rows.candidateFullMixedExact: Sheba sebaka sa hao pele u khetha moo o ka behang tender crops, trees, or buildings.
rows.reason: “before choosing” is retained and the locative wording says where to place the listed objects; tender crops, trees, and buildings remain exact source English.

rows.sourceEnglishExact: A wall or shade cloth can shade a bed longer in winter than in summer. Check the actual shadows before you build or fix a shade structure in place.

currentLearnerExact.text: A wall or shade cloth can shade a bed longer in winter than in summer. Hlahloba shadows tsa sebele before you build or fix a shade structure in place.

rows.candidateFullMixedExact: A wall or shade cloth can shade a bed longer in winter than in summer. Hlahloba shadows tsa sebele pele o haha kapa o lokisa shade structure sebakeng sa yona.
rows.proposedFullMixedRepair: A wall or shade cloth can shade a bed longer in winter than in summer. Hlahloba shadows tsa sebele before you build or fix a shade structure in place.
rows.reason: The translated “fix in place” verb can read as repair/adjust/arrange rather than install or secure at the chosen position. Keep the complete source action and its before condition in English; the localized actual-shadow check remains before that action. The winter-versus-summer possibility (“can … longer”) is preserved exactly in source English.
